question: Compare Supabase and AWS RDS on managed PostgreSQL features and pricing.

search_results.content: Supabase offers a managed Postgres database with built-in auth, realtime subscriptions, and an edge functions layer starting with a generous free tier and flat-rate pro pricing at $25/month. AWS RDS provides traditional managed PostgreSQL with fine-grained VPC configuration, multi-AZ high availability options, and instance-based pay-as-you-go pricing without built-in backend-as-a-service features.

expected_facts: Supabase includes built-in authentication and realtime features with a $25/month pro tier.
AWS RDS offers fine-grained VPC configuration and instance-based pay-as-you-go pricing.
RDS lacks native backend-as-a-service features like built-in edge functions or real-time pub/sub.

question: What are the core differences in routing and data fetching between Next.js App Router and Remix?

search_results.content: Next.js App Router uses React Server Components (RSC) by default with file-system routing inside the app directory, fetching data directly inside server components via async/await. Remix relies on standard document requests, nested routing where parent and child loaders fetch data in parallel, and action functions handling mutations.

expected_facts: Next.js App Router defaults to React Server Components with direct async/await data fetching in server components.
Remix utilizes nested routing with parallel loader functions for data fetching and action functions for mutations.
Next.js uses file-system routing in the app directory while Remix uses standard route module conventions.
